predecessors.name: Tokugawa shogunate
predecessors.text: the whole shogunate, handed to the Meiji state by the Restoration of 3 January 1868

predecessors.name: Republic of Ezo
predecessors.text: Ezo, where the Republic proclaimed on 27 January 1869 surrendered on 26-27 June 1869 (Republic of Ezo page; the Empire page says the siege of Hakodate ended in May 1869)

ledger.x: 1868: the Meiji Restoration of 3 January 1868 begins the Empire of Japan, with Kyoto as its capital.
1868: the Meiji state inherits the shogunate's undivided Sakhalin.
1868: the war opens and the shogunate's remaining land is contested.
1868: the north is the shogunate's land, drawn contested from the first month for lack of a front line.
1868: the Edo front ends.
1868: the Kanto and the rest of Cliopatria's remainder pass wholly to the Meiji state after Ueno (4 July 1868).
1868: the Northern Alliance is crushed.
1868: Tohoku and Niigata pass to the Meiji state with the fall of Aizu (6 November 1868).
1869: the capital moves from Kyoto to Tokyo.
1869: the Republic of Ezo holds Hokkaido.
1869: the Republic of Ezo surrenders.
1869: Ezo passes wholly to the Meiji state with the surrender of 26-27 June 1869.
1872: the kingdom becomes a domain of the Empire of Japan, mirrored from the ryukyu-kingdom dossier.
1876: Japan takes the Bonin Islands.
1877: Sakhalin becomes wholly Russian.
1877: the whole Kuril chain becomes Japanese.
1879: the Ryukyu Domain is abolished, mirrored from the ryukyu-kingdom dossier.
1879: Japan abolishes the Ryukyu Domain and makes the islands Okinawa Prefecture.
1895: China cedes Taiwan and the Penghu Islands at Shimonoseki.
1895: China cedes the Liaodong Peninsula at Shimonoseki (17 April 1895).
1895: Japan gives Liaodong back after the Triple Intervention.
1905: Korea becomes a Japanese protectorate.
1905: southern Sakhalin passes to Japan at Portsmouth.
1905: Japan takes over Russia's lease of the Liaodong tip.
1910: the Korean protectorate ends in annexation, 29 August 1910.
1910: Japan annexes Korea.
1915: Japan holds the German islands of Micronesia.
1914: Japan occupies the German leased territory at Tsingtao.
1918: Japanese troops land at Vladivostok and occupy the Maritime Provinces.
1920: the League of Nations takes over the Micronesian islands for Japan.
1920: the South Seas Mandate.
1920: Japan occupies northern Sakhalin.
1920: the owner's label changes; the occupation does not end.
1920: the Japanese occupation of the Maritime Provinces continues against the Far Eastern Republic, whose territory included 'the Maritime Province'.
1922: Japan leaves Primorye and Siberia.
1922: the Far Eastern Republic is 'Disestablished: 15 November 1922' (joined to Soviet Russia).
1922: the occupation ends with the return of the territory.
1922: Tsingtao goes to China ('returned to China on 10 December 1922').
1922: the occupation of northern Sakhalin continues against the new Soviet Union.
1925: northern Sakhalin is evacuated.
1931: Japan invades Manchuria.
1932: the occupied Manchuria becomes the puppet state of Manchukuo.
1932: Manchukuo is proclaimed, a Japanese client.
1933: Rehe is added to Manchukuo.
1935: the Japanese-backed East Hebei government is declared.
1936: the Mongol military government is formed under Japanese patronage.
1937: Beiping and Tianjin fall after the Marco Polo Bridge incident of 7 July 1937.
1937: Shanghai falls in November and Nanjing in December.
1938: East Hebei ends.
1938: Japan holds North China.
1938: Kaifeng falls.
1938: Wuhan is abandoned.
1938: Japan takes the Guangdong coast.
1939: Japan invades Hainan.
1941: northern Vietnam is occupied.
1941: Hong Kong falls.
1941: Guam is seized.
1941: Guam and Wake are seized.
1942: the Dutch East Indies.
1942: Rabaul falls, 23 January.
1942: Japan invades the Solomon Islands in January 1942 ('Japan invaded the Solomon Islands in January 1942').
1942: Malaya, Borneo and Singapore.
1942: Japan invades Timor.

1942: Burma. 'The Japanese captured Moulmein on 31 January 1942' and 'On 8 March, the Japanese occupied Rangoon'. The whole country is my reading; Cliopatria draws it in 1943. Ba Maw was 'wartime President of Burma under the Japanese'.
1942: Japan occupies the Andaman Islands.
1942: the Philippines.
1942: Japan lands on Attu.
1942: Japan lands on Kiska (6 June 1942), the day before Attu; see the Attu event.
1943: the United States retakes Attu.
1943: Japan leaves Kiska.
1944: Operation Ichi-Go takes the rest of Henan.
1944: Ichi-Go reaches Hunan.
1944: the United States retakes Guam.
1944: Ichi-Go enters Guangxi.
1945: the Kuril Islands pass to the Soviet Union.
1945: the Kwantung Leased Territory, 'a Japanese colony occupied by the Soviet Union 1945–1955'.
1945: Korea north of the 38th parallel goes to Soviet authority ('Japanese Korea north of the 38th parallel north' under Soviet authority).
1945: Korea south of the 38th parallel goes to US authority ('Japanese Korea south of the 38th parallel north' under US authority).
1945: Taiwan goes to Chinese authority ('Japanese Taiwan' under Republic of China authority).
1945: the South Seas Mandate is 'occupied by the United States, 1945–1947'.
1945: the Ryukyu Islands under US control.
1945: the Amami Islands under US administration, 'until 1953'.
1945: the Nanpo Islands and Iwo Jima under US administration, returned in 1968.
1945: the Japanese take the rest of Indochina from the French.
1945: the Soviet invasion ends Manchukuo.
1945: Rehe goes with Manchukuo (August 1945).
1945: the Soviets take Karafuto.
1945: Mengjiang ends.
1945: the islands are surrendered.
1945: the Allied occupation of Japan begins, 'from the surrender of the Empire of Japan on September 2, 1945'.
1945: Japan 'formally surrendered on 2 September 1945'; China 'regained' Taiwan and the lands lost since 1895.

wars.name: Boshin War
wars.outcome: Meiji victory: Edo surrendered in May 1868 (Ueno, 4 July), Aizu 'finally admitted defeat on November 6' 1868, and Enomoto surrendered at Hakodate on 26-27 June 1869, ending the Republic of Ezo.

wars.name: First Sino-Japanese War
wars.outcome: Japanese victory; the Treaty of Shimonoseki (17 April 1895) cedes Taiwan, Penghu and Liaodong and recognises Korea's independence; Liaodong is returned in November 1895 after the Triple Intervention.

wars.name: Russo-Japanese War
wars.outcome: Japanese victory; the Treaty of Portsmouth (5 September 1905) gives southern Sakhalin and the Liaodong lease to Japan and Japan's paramount interests in Korea.

wars.name: Japanese capture of the German colonies
wars.outcome: Micronesia held from 1914 and mandated to Japan in 1920; Tsingtao held from 7 November 1914 and returned to China on 10 December 1922.

wars.name: Siberian intervention
wars.outcome: Withdrawal from Siberia and Primorye in October 1922; northern Sakhalin evacuated in 1925 on the opening of relations with the Soviet Union.

wars.name: Japanese invasion of Manchuria
wars.outcome: Manchukuo is established on 1 March 1932; Rehe is taken in 1933 and the Tanggu Truce 'gave Japan control of Rehe Province'.

wars.name: Second Sino-Japanese War
wars.outcome: Japan holds the coastal and northern cities; the front is static from 1939 to Ichi-Go in 1944; Japan 'formally surrendered on 2 September 1945'.

wars.name: Pacific War
wars.outcome: Japan overruns South-East Asia in the first six months of 1942, is stopped at Midway (June 1942), and 'surrendered unconditionally on 15 August and signed a surrender document on 2 September' 1945.

wars.name: Soviet–Japanese War
wars.outcome: Soviet victory: Karafuto, the Kurils, Manchuria and the Kwantung territory pass to Soviet authority.

certainty.note: The Sakhalin line is undivided and the Boshin War fronts are three coarse zones (Kanto, Tohoku, Ezo); the sea coasts of the home islands are sharp, the Ryukyu relation is the ryukyu-kingdom dossier's.
Fixed by treaty: the Kuril-Sakhalin exchange (1875-77), Shimonoseki (1895), Portsmouth (1905), the annexation of Korea (1910), the League mandate (1920).
Manchukuo, Mengjiang and the occupied Chinese and South-East Asian lands have no surveyed lines; the home islands, Taiwan, Korea and Karafuto (the 50th parallel) stay sharp.
The postwar outline is the coast.
